15th Edition  ·  Rome, Italy

Video Dev Days 2026

16th – 18th October, 2026  ·  Sapienza University of Rome

The Open Multimedia Conference!

About

The VideoLAN non-profit organization is excited to invite you to the upcoming multimedia open-source event in Rome!

In this edition, participants from the VideoLAN and open-source multimedia communities will gather in Rome, Italy to discuss and collaborate on advancing the future of open-source multimedia.

This technical conference will focus on in-depth multimedia topics, including codecs and their implementations such as x264 and dav1d, as well as frameworks like FFmpeg, and projects like VideoLAN, VLC, Kodi, libplacebo, mpv and related projects.

This event is specifically geared towards the technical aspects of multimedia, emphasizing low-level components like codecs, their implementations, frameworks, playback libraries, and various innovative projects within the multimedia domain.

When ?

October 16th - 18th, 2026

Where ?

Rome, Italy

For ?

Anyone who cares about open source multimedia technologies and development.

From ?

VideoLAN. But you are very welcome to co-sponsor the event.

Call for Proposals

Send a title and a paragraph — that is the whole process!

All of these were real talks at previous VDDs:

Checkasm|dav1d update|Multithreading in FFmpeg|llvm-mingw|Reading bits faster in libavcodec|x265 update|Libswscale Reimagined|What is HDR?|The pointer provenance problem in C|Hijacking AI CPU extension for multimedia|KODI updates|Tools for Screen Sharing in AV1|rav1e update|Ensuring the future of assembly language programming|FFGlitch|Why VFX Cares About Codecs|RV and RVV Introduction|State of the ffmpeg CLI & MV-HEVC decoding|VLC Android Technical Stack|Debugging assembly functions|Compression for Virtual Production|APV codec|One Checkasm to rule them all|Reverse engineering popular and dead codecs|Dynamic Filter Loading at Meta|Re-using AV1 for SfM|IAMF|SVT-AV1-PSY: Origins, Features, and Future|Enabling Intelligent Media Playback on RISC-V|AMD AMF and Streaming SDK|VLC 4.0

WHAT MAKES A TALK

Media stack

Highly technical engineering relevant to the open multimedia stack, codecs, playback libraries, or hardware acceleration.

WHO SENDS ONE

Anyone.

Maintainers, students, first-timers, industry engineers, or independent hackers with code and insights to share.

WHAT TO SEND

An abstract.

Title, short description, expected duration, and your bio. Nobody has ever been told their talk was too specific!

Main Track: Saturday & Sunday (17–18 October) · Lightning talks open Friday (16 October)

Proposals deadline: 1 October 2026

Submit a Proposal via Form

Awesome Samples Competition

2nd Edition · The Derek Challenge · The Most Cursed Media File

Make the weirdest media file you can — standards abuse, not random corruption!

WAY I

Technically Valid

No player will touch it.

Strictly conformant with the specification, yet exploiting obscure, forgotten, or extreme corner cases that break every known decoder.

WAY II

Technically Invalid

Plays anyway.

Violates specs, combines forbidden structures, or corrupts logic, yet VLC, mpv, or ffplay somehow manage to render it.

Ingeniosus

Clever

Maledictus

Cursed

Functionalis

Functional

Impossibilis

Impossible

The Three Competition Rules

Rule 01

Explainable

You must be able to explain how the file works and what mechanism is triggered.

Rule 02

No Exploits

Memory corruption, security exploits, crashes, or resource exhaustion do not count.

Rule 03

Reproducible

Must be 100% reproducible from your provided script, toolchain, or recipe.

“We want undefined behaviour in the specification, not in the heap.”

Code of Conduct

This community activity is running under the VideoLAN Code of Conduct. We expect all attendees to respect our Shared Values.

Contact

The Video Dev Days are organized by the board members of the VideoLAN non-profit organization, Jean-Baptiste Kempf, Thomas Guillem, Denis Charmet, Felix Paul Kühne, Vibhoothi and Konstantin Pavlov. You can reach us at board@videolan.org.
